Anna,

Appreciate the clarity. Attaching a concise playbook draft that maps our operational controls to NIST AI RMF functions and an EU Act note that classifies likely high-risk surfaces for a health-care customer and the mitigation layers we apply.

Quick summary:
- NIST mapping: we enumerate activities in Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond but frame them around the AI RMF core (Map, Govern, Measure, Manage). For each activity we list owners (Product, Security, Applied ML), evidence artifacts (audit logs, model card, eval snapshot), and automatic triggers that create a rollback or canary (perf/regression thresholds, privacy drift).
- EU Act: we provide class-level logic (e.g., automatic triage & diagnosis assistance => high-risk 3.2b), mandatory documentation (technical documentation + high-level risk assessment), and operational mitigations (private deployment option + KMS, restricted PII logging).
- Evaluation/regression: we run pre-deploy gated checks (functional regression on a holdout prompt set, safety filters, distributional shift monitors) and post-deploy continuous monitoring with rolling snapshots. If any critical metric regresses (configurable, default: >2% degradation in top-1 intent accuracy or flagged safety hits), automatic traffic split/break-glass to previous version and pager.

I sent three attachments: redwood_model-risk-playbook_v1.pdf (one-page mapping + appendix), nist-eu-control-mapping.xlsx (detailed control matrix), and eval-regression-plan.xlsx (test harness + trigger matrix).

We put Rishi and Marissa on the thread to add technical detail where you need it.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Anna — adding the technical mapping and specifics you can drop into the RFP: 

1) NIST AI RMF -> Redwood controls (high level):
   - Map: model inventory & provenance (model_id, version, training-date, weights-fingerprint). We produce signed model manifests stored in object storage with digest + code hash.
   - Govern: role-based deployment gating (canary policies, rollout windows), audit trails for config changes (immutable changelog).
   - Measure: automated eval suite, drift detectors (KL/divergence on token distribution + metric monitors), safety signal aggregation (user reports, automated filters).
   - Manage: incident playbooks, automated rollback + fallback routing to lower-cost vetted model, and postmortem artifacts.

2) EU AI Act classification note (short):
   - For clinical triage / diagnostic assistance: falls into high-risk medical devices category depending on intended use. We recommend a joint assessment — Redwood supports private deployments + audit logging and can provide the technical documentation required (system architecture, data flows, performance metrics).

3) Regression/eval specifics you asked about:
   - Pre-release: deterministic unit tests, functional eval (1000+ prompts seeded from your annotated prompt bank), safety policy checks, and benchmark suite (latency, throughput, accuracy).
   - Post-release: continuous sampling (1 in 1000 requests snapshot), nightly offline replay + compare against baseline, and weekly aggregated dashboards. Alerts tiered: P1 safety hits -> immediate rollback; P2 performance drop -> canary & ops review.

I included a short checklist in the spreadsheet for each artifact you can request during procurement (model_card, eval_snapshot, changelog, regression_report).

Happy to walk through line-by-line over a 30-minute call.

-Rishi
Principal Applied Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@medicore.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarifying scope for model risk mapping – RFP section 3

Hi Anna — adding the evaluation and regression play specifics from the product/ops side so procurement has concrete SLAs and artifacts: 

- Eval harness: we version the prompt sets and label schema in a Git-backed repo. Each model change triggers a CI job that runs the harness (unit + integration + safety scans). CI produces an eval_snapshot.json, diff report, and an artifacts zip.
- Regression thresholds: configurable per-customer. Typical defaults we propose: intent accuracy delta >2% (stat sig), safety violation increase >0.5% absolute, or a 15% degradation in median latency under baseline load.
- Rollout policy: staged rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on P1 or manual hold on P2. We retain traces for 30 days by default (extendable per contract).
- Evidence package for audits: model_card.pdf, eval_snapshot.zip, changelog.txt, and deployment manifests. For EU Act support we can provide a HLA (high level assessment) template for you to sign off.

I've also put together a short sample eviction/rollback log in the attached spreadsheet (eval-regression-plan.xlsx) to show the exact fields you would receive.

If those defaults look ok, we can include them in the commercial SOW and have legal reference them in the Compliance Appendix.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
